ironcasting.page.spells.title: Spells From ISS
ironcasting.page.spells.0: I have discovered some magical scrolls that can cast amazing spells called 'Iron Magic'. Even more surprisingly, these scrolls can be read by the Scribe's Insight and cast using Hexcasting methods, just like those scrolls with hex patterns!
ironcasting.page.spells.1: Most of these patterns only accept a single real number between 1 and 10 on the stack top as the intensity parameter. The spell strength is calculated as the direct scroll casting strength multiplied by this intensity parameter, while the amethyst dust consumption equals the original mana consumption multiplied by (intensity parameter squared).$(br)In some cases, an intensity parameter greater than one serves no purpose other than wasting media.$(br)Additionally, note that casting these spells multiple times within the same game tick will consume additional media. Specifically, the nth casting consumes n times the normal media cost.
ironcasting.page.spells.2: Some patterns require additional parameters to cast.$(br)Acupuncture, Blessing of Life, Blight, Chain Lightning, Devour, Root, Sacrifice, Wololo, Slow, Haste require a living entity beneath the intensity parameter in addition to the top stack intensity parameter.$(br)Wisp and Firefly Swarm require a stack structure like this to cast: (target entity, spawn coordinates, intensity parameter).
ironcasting.page.spells.3: Acid Spit, Ball Lightning, Fire Arrow, Fireball, Firebolt, Guiding Bolt, Icicle, Lightning Lance, Lob Creeper, Magic Arrow, Magic Missile, Magma Bomb, Poison Arrow, Snowball, Wither Skull need a stack in the format of (vec1, vec2, num) to cast, where vec1 refers to where the projectile will spawn, vec2's direction refers to shoot direction while length refers to shoot speed (will cost extra media if length > 1), num is the intensity parameter.$(br)It seems nature has held something back, and some patterns may not function properly. What a sad thing.
ironcasting.page.spells.4: You may have noticed that I've been calling the Iotas read from these scrolls 'patterns', but they actually seem to be 'images'. I once wrote the read Iotas onto regular scrolls, and they were indeed patterns, but these patterns had overlapping strokes which made them impossible to draw with a staff. Looking at scrolls with such patterns gave me eye strain, so it's better not to do this.
